components.gap: The success condition's 'construction or argument' and 'full treatment promised by its declared status' (proved=annex:p15.huber.tv.pair) are not met for the k_+ direction. The theorem asserts unique k_- and k_+ (body 125-130). The proof writes continuity, monotonicity and strict increase only for g(k)=int(ks-p1)_+ (annex 134-144). For the upper-transfer function it says only 'The decreasing upper-transfer function int(p1-ks)_+dmu has the analogous property' (annex 145-146). Its endpoint values (1 at k=0, 0 at k=1), its strict decrease where positive, and any stated reduction to the proved g case (int(p1-ks)_+ = int((1-k)s-p0)_+) are not written. The existence and uniqueness of k_+ therefore rest on 'similarly', which reproduces the source's own deferral on p.1758 instead of completing it. Failure condition 'missing promised direction/case' holds. Also unwritten: the proof's 'lower region' and 'upper region' (annex 156-167) are never defined or shown to equal {r<c'} and {r>c''} on the pair's support. That identification is the step that makes l=max{c',min(c'',r)}=q1/q0.

components.gap: The success condition requires the entry's 'hypotheses'. The failure condition 'unstated assumption' holds. The entry never states its observation space. The setting it invokes allows an arbitrary measurable space (body 13-14), and the chapter's closing lines (353-354) assert that no observation support was narrowed. Yet the displayed identity sup_{R in H_1} E_R N_{a,b} = E_{Q_1} N_{a,b} = (1-(3/5)^r)/(2/5) depends on the space being X={0,1}. So do the proof steps 'its mass p at one ranges over [2/5,3/5]' and 'If no such observation has occurred by time r, the test exits at the lower boundary' (annex 487-514). If X has any further point x*, the chapter's convention (r=1 off the nominal supports) gives score 4/5 there. The allowed contamination H=delta_{x*} then gives P_R(N_{3c,b}>3)=(3/5)^3*(1-(2/3)^3)=19/125>0=P_{Q_1}(N_{3c,b}>3). The supremum then exceeds E_{Q_1}N. The hypothesis on which the headline display rests is therefore not supplied.

defect_observations.observation: The observation space is unstated. The sup-over-H_1 identity holds only on X={0,1}, as the 19/125 counterexample in the component gap shows. This also conflicts with the chapter's closing statement (353-354) that no observation support was narrowed. Other examples state their spaces ({a,b,c} at RHT body 267; {0,1,2,...} at RSE body 289).

k_+ existence and uniqueness rest on 'has the analogous property' (145-146). 'lower region' and 'upper region' are used without definition or identification with {r<c'}, {r>c''} (156-167). The later proofs of thm:p15-huber-stochastic-order (annex 196-204) and thm:p15-robust-testing-calculation rely on that identification.

The lemma asserts that infinite entropy 'can also occur with equivalent laws and finite scores everywhere'. Its declared proof (annex 4-48) neither argues this nor cites thm:p15-infinite-entropy-finite-scores (body 288-316), the only place it is shown. The verdict counts that later example; a cross-reference is missing.

Two negative assertions have no argument in the declared proof (annex 222-276) and no cross-reference: 'boundary divergence is sufficient, not necessary' and 'Equality of two infinite means does not imply that conclusion'. Both are shown only in thm:p15-singular-contamination-stopping (body 337-347; annex 523-532). The parts of that example used here do not depend on the D1 defect.

The body claim 'at the overlap boundary the maximin power is still only the test's level' (body 262-263) has no argument in annex 347-391. It is the e=e* case of thm:p15-robust-overlap (body 65-72), which the annex does not cite.

The equalizer threshold's existence asserts quantile bracketing and says it 'follows directly from the inverse-CDF construction', with the two-line derivation from q_F(u)<=z iff u<=F(z) unwritten. The alternative 'same continuity argument as thm:p15-likelihood-threshold' does not apply verbatim: that lemma covers finite thresholds of L under P_0, and its proof uses L finite P_0-a.s. (hypothesis-tests annex 22-60). Under the mixture M, T_n=infinity can carry mass. Accepted because the cited proved construction yields the bracketing directly.

The alternative side is given by 'in the same proof' (651), 'the same calculation' (681) and 'identical reasoning' (694). Accepted only because each line displays the substituted moment inequality (E_{R1}e^{-gamma}<=1; E_{R1}gamma>=kappa_1) and the resulting bound (e^A; e^A(1+|A|/B)+C/B).

That the cross-product condition makes the extended endpoint ratio nondecreasing on S is asserted with 'implies' (524-525). The one-sided-support cases behind the promised 'varying supports' are not written: e.g. p0(x)=0<p0(y) with x<y is excluded by the inequality. The transfer of the sequential theorems to the union classes (560-562) rests on a one-sentence dependency statement.

The one-sided support cases are given by 'The same calculation directly from the densities covers ...', with one sub-case worked (v>0, p0=0<p1). Accepted because the displayed division by p0>0 covers p1=0<p0 verbatim and the zero-contamination outcomes are stated.

The sequential path comparison couples infinitely many increments by citing the n-coordinate construction of thm:p15-robust-product-order. The infinite sequence of independent uniforms is not mentioned here; RSE annex 227 states it.

The level-alpha problem is posed as A<=alpha, but Huber's problem (ii) (printed p.1754) constrains the loss-weighted null risk L_0*A<=alpha. The problems are equivalent after rescaling alpha, but the text does not say so.
